$comment: The most each public page may ship on its first load, in bytes, compressed (gzip for text; fonts as served), by kind and in total. scripts/check-performance-budget.mjs measures the built output against it on every pull request (Checks, 'Public site checks'), from the files a page's own HTML names, not from a timed run, and fails naming the page and the kind. scripts/performance-budget.mjs says what counts as first load. Each limit was set on 2026-11-23 from what the build then shipped (re-set the same day after the audit fixes to the styles and the pages heads), plus 5%, rounded up to 100 bytes: a budget holds a page where it is, it does not say the page is light enough (lane A makes the heavy ones lighter, and lowers the limits as it does). To raise a limit, say why in the pull request. node scripts/check-performance-budget.mjs --propose prints the numbers for the build in front of it.
